newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end listless trade mixed but steady.
newsitem.headline: German shares end listless trade mixed but steady.

text.p: German shares end the day steadier on Monday, having treaded water over the day as the U.S. Labor Day holiday scuppered hopes of the IBIS DAX index finding new impetus to forge any meaningful gains.
The IBIS DAX index, which tracks all-day electronic trade in German shares, ended the day up 3.85 points, or 0.15 percent, higher at 2,538.34 points.
Earlier, bourse trade ended with the DAX index, which gauges trade in 30 German blue-chip stocks, down 10.95 points, or 0.43 percent, at 2,532.88 points.

A slightly firmer dollar helped offset the effect of lower German bonds, but the U.S. currency was still way off its highs of several weeks ago and did not provide any real inspiration in trade generally lacking direction.
Carmaker Volkswagen AG was hit by a newspaper report on Friday of problems with cars produced at its Wolfsburg plant.
Volkswagen ended bourse down 6.30 marks at 543.70 marks, but recovered slightly in afternoon trade after it denied the report to close the day down 4.90 marks at 543.80 marks.
Shares in mixed utility Veba AG were boosted at bourse open by reports that it was planning a deal with gas company Ruhrgas on use of Ruhrgas' cable network for Veba's telecoms business.
However, Veba shares ended bourse trade 41 pfennigs lower at 77.24 marks in line with the market and ended the day down 45 pfennigs at 77.15 marks.
German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG ended bourse trade 2.20 marks lower at 208.30 marks after German cartel authorities confirmed they were looking into its pricing structure on domestic flights.
Lufthansa recovered to end the day up 45 pfennigs at 208.25 marks.
